_note: Run: <torch-venv>/bin/python bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/mae-backbone.json --python <torch-venv>/bin/python (an interpreter with torch, so the backbone builds and loads in-process). This is the A3:mae wiring (docs/STEP3_PORTING_PLAN.md): MAE reused as a frozen spatial-backbone kind for the ARSSL harness. The MAE-specific provider lives in the method's own directory (methods/25_mae/downstream_backbone.py) and the shared layer (downstream/spatial_backbones.py) DISCOVERS it, naming no method. These guards prove the wiring is not vacuous -- a checkpoint that is not this MAE is refused (both directions: alien keys and missing encoder weights), the CLS prefix is dropped so the spatial grid is the patch tokens alone, the backbone stays frozen in eval, the kind is both discovered into KINDS and actually dispatched (not an accept-anything), and the structural provider detector requires a real build (not just a KIND).
